weather.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 10 at 3:25PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
weather.area: Northern Wasatch Front; Salt Lake Valley; Wasatch Back; Wasatch Mountains I-80 North
weather.text:
At 325 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
Salt Lake City, moving northeast at 45 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Salt Lake City, West Valley City, Bountiful, Morgan, South Salt
Lake, North Salt Lake, Centerville, Woods Cross, West Bountiful,
Emigration Canyon, East Canyon State Park, Canyon Rim, Millcreek,
Salt Lake City International Airport, Henefer and Portersville.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 84 between mile markers 104 and 113. Interstate 80 in Utah
between mile markers 114 and 119...and between mile markers 123 and
126. Interstate 15 between mile markers 303 and 319.
weather.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

weather.headline: Flood Watch issued October 10 at 4:07AM MDT until October 12 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
weather.area: Great Salt Lake Desert and Mountains; Tooele and Rush Valleys; Eastern Box Elder County; Northern Wasatch Front; Salt Lake Valley; Utah Valley; Cache Valley/Utah Portion; Wasatch Back; Bear Lake and Bear River Valley; Wasatch Mountains I-80 North; Wasatch Mountains South of I-80; Western Uinta Mountains; Western Uinta Basin; Western Millard and Juab Counties
weather.text:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Western
Millard and Juab Counties, Bear Lake and Bear River Valley, Cache
Valley/Utah Portion, Eastern Box Elder County, Great Salt Lake
Desert and Mountains, Northern Wasatch Front, Salt Lake Valley,
Tooele and Rush Valleys, Utah Valley, Wasatch Back, Wasatch
Mountains I-80 North, Wasatch Mountains South of I-80, Western
Uinta Basin and Western Uinta Mountains. This includes recent burn
scars such as Rocky Canyon.

* WHEN...From late tonight through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and recent burn scars. Flooding may occur in poor
drainage and urban areas. Extensive street flooding and flooding of
creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Moisture associated with the remnan
weather.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

weather.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 10 at 4:01AM MDT until October 11 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
weather.area: Great Salt Lake Desert and Mountains; Tooele and Rush Valleys; Eastern Box Elder County; Northern Wasatch Front; Salt Lake Valley; Utah Valley; Cache Valley/Utah Portion; Wasatch Back; Bear Lake and Bear River Valley; Sanpete Valley
weather.text:
* WHAT...South winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.

* WHERE...The Wasatch Front, Great Salt Lake Desert and Mountains,
Tooele and Rush Valleys, Cache Valley/Utah Portion, Wasatch Back,
Bear Lake and Bear River Valley, and Sanpete Valley.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM MDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result.
weather.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles and vehicles with trailers. Use extra caution.

Secure outdoor objects.
